prompt: Some people say it is important to protect all wild animals. Others, however, say it is only important to protect some wild animals, not all of them. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay:
Some people argue that every wild animal deserves protection, regardless of its population or economic value. Others believe that limited resources should be directed only towards endangered or particularly important species. While both perspectives have merit, I firmly believe that conserving all wild animals is the most effective way to maintain ecological balance and safeguard the natural world.

Those who support protecting only certain species often point to practical considerations. Governments and conservation organisations operate under financial constraints, making it impossible to save every animal. As a result, they argue that priority should be given to endangered species or animals that play a crucial ecological role, such as pollinators or apex predators. By concentrating funding and scientific expertise on these species, conservation efforts may produce more immediate and measurable results.

Nevertheless, I believe that all wild animals should be protected because every species contributes to the stability of its ecosystem. Even animals that appear insignificant may regulate populations, disperse seeds, or support food chains in ways that are not fully understood. The disappearance of a single species can trigger unforeseen consequences that ultimately threaten biodiversity and human well-being. For example, the decline of insects in many countries has negatively affected crop pollination, highlighting the interconnected nature of ecosystems. Protecting wildlife as a whole is therefore a preventative strategy rather than simply a response to extinction.

In conclusion, although prioritising selected species may seem financially sensible, I believe this approach is too narrow. Every wild animal has ecological value, whether obvious or hidden, and preserving biodiversity requires comprehensive protection. In the long term, conserving all wildlife is not only an environmental responsibility but also an essential investment in the health and sustainability of our planet.
